lead.headline: Up 61.6 and finished; Tate's 1.6 and Monday's Rams keep it a coin flip
lead.deck: Golden scored 20.3 on your bench, Strange outscored Loveland by 9.9, Barkley was inactive, and their two best players are still to come.
lead.body: Start with the bad news about your own players. Carnell Tate was active against the defence that allows receivers the most and caught one of five targets for 1.6; no injury or exit was reported, and Matthew Golden, the coin flip the projection put behind him, scored 20.3 on your bench. Colston Loveland scored 3.9 from two backup quarterbacks while Brenton Strange, whom you swapped out for him on Wednesday, scored 13.8. Jonathan Taylor was held to 45 yards and 11.2 in a game Indianapolis chased. Saquon Barkley was inactive in London with no new date. Alvin Kamara had five touches that nobody has explained. In all, 22.3 points stayed on the bench. The result so far: 113.4 to 51.8, and you are done except for Jason Myers. George Pickens, 28.0 on Thursday, Garrett Wilson, 23.4, and Trevor Lawrence, 20.7, carried it. Three theses were graded: Tuten over Barkley closed right, Tuten over Gordon lost by 3.2, and the Loveland swap lost by 9.9. What is left to play is theirs. Goff, Jeremiyah Love and Kittle were in progress, and Kyren Williams and Puka Nacua, projected for 39.6 together, play Buffalo on Monday night. ESPN has it 118.0 to 116.1 and gives you 53%. Next week's injuries to watch are Jacksonville's left tackle, carted off in front of Lawrence and Tuten, and the Philadelphia backfield, where Shipley left hurt and nobody is left behind Barkley. Marvin Harrison Jr. was traded to Houston after the games and is on waivers until Wednesday.
